about: The menu of number kinds for the one-pagers (rule 14). Every page fills the same kinds; 'general' kinds are about every addiction and are shown the same on every page. 'pick' marks the kinds recommended for the prototype; the owner's marks on the review page can swap them. 'where' is the page section a picked kind shows in (rule 15: hope first, then beliefs and the graph, then more numbers). 'reader' lists the severity tags a number of this kind may carry (RULEBOOK rule 3).

kinds.label: Already free, counted
kinds.question: Of people who were ever hooked, how many are already free, counted, not projected?
kinds.why: Rule 10: the cautious estimate first. A head count is harder to doubt than a lifetime projection.

kinds.label: Free in a lifetime, projected
kinds.question: What share of people ever hooked are projected to get free in their lifetime?
kinds.why: His original hero (90.6% for alcohol). Kept as the hero's second line, marked as a projection that likely runs high.

kinds.label: Years until half are free
kinds.question: How long after it started were half of them free?
kinds.why: Projection from recalled ages; reviewers say it likely runs hopeful. In the menu, not picked.

kinds.label: Age when it ended
kinds.question: How old were people, on average, when the problem ended?
kinds.why: He liked 'about 38' for alcohol (5 Nov).

kinds.label: What came with getting free
kinds.question: Which life changes made getting free more likely?
kinds.why: A link, not a cause; useful for some readers. In the menu, not picked.

kinds.label: Quit with no treatment
kinds.question: Of people who got free, how many never used treatment, a group or medicine?
kinds.why: He wants to see who quits using what (4 Nov).

kinds.label: Tries it took
kinds.question: How many serious tries did it take people who got free?
kinds.why: Answers 'I've failed before, so I'll fail again'.

kinds.label: All at once or step by step
kinds.question: Did people stop all at once or cut down first, and which worked?
kinds.why: In the menu, not picked: on most pages it overlaps with stop-or-cut-down.

kinds.label: How often the first try slips
kinds.question: How many slip on a try, and when?
kinds.why: Part of 'How quitting goes', which he liked (5 Nov). A slip is normal, shown with when it happens.

kinds.label: Stop fully or cut down
kinds.question: For people who were hooked, how did stopping fully compare with cutting down?
kinds.why: Rule 4: the moderation question answered only with numbers about addicts. The alcohol '27% vs 7%' is the model.

kinds.label: The best-tested medicine
kinds.question: What does the best-tested medicine do: how many in 100 stay off with it, and how many without it?
kinds.why: Shown as 'X in 100 with it vs Y in 100 without' (rule 12a), so it reads on the first pass.

kinds.label: Talk therapy or groups
kinds.question: What does the best-tested therapy or group do?
kinds.why: Help is optional and a tool (his plan step 5); readers want to know if it is worth it.

kinds.label: Getting help early
kinds.question: Did people who got help early do better later?
kinds.why: Picked after the first review: '62% vs 43%' was one of the v10 'How quitting goes' numbers he liked. Not a trial, and it says so.

kinds.label: Something on the line
kinds.question: Does a reward for staying off help?
kinds.why: Strong for nicotine and weed; in the menu, not picked.

kinds.label: What the first month gives back
kinds.question: What measurably changes in the first weeks off?
kinds.why: Part of 'How quitting goes', which he liked. A heavy-user number is allowed here with its tag shown.

kinds.label: Mood after quitting
kinds.question: How do mood, anxiety or life satisfaction change after quitting?
kinds.why: Answers 'life will be empty without it'.

kinds.label: Sleep after quitting
kinds.question: When does sleep come back?
kinds.why: Often already in the timeline; in the menu, not picked.

kinds.label: Body and sex
kinds.question: What changes in the body, sex or weight?
kinds.why: Picked after the first review: the v10 'How quitting goes' numbers he liked include body changes (nicotine: erections, weight).

kinds.label: Alcohol and drugs pooled: tries it took
kinds.question: Across alcohol and drugs, how many serious tries did it take?
kinds.why: The same on every page (rule 14), labelled as every addiction together.

kinds.label: Alcohol and drugs pooled: quit with no treatment
kinds.question: Across alcohol and drugs, how many got free without any help?
kinds.why: The same on every page.

kinds.label: Alcohol and drugs pooled: life keeps getting better
kinds.question: How does life go in the years after?
kinds.why: The same on every page.

kinds.label: Still hooked, or not, years later
kinds.question: Of people who were once hooked, how many are still hooked now, and how many ever had treatment?
kinds.why: Kept from the v10 'How quitting goes' numbers he liked (alcohol: only 1 in 4 still hooked).

kinds.label: How many get withdrawal, and when it peaks
kinds.question: How many get withdrawal symptoms when they stop, and when are they worst?
kinds.why: Kept from the v10 'How quitting goes' numbers he liked (weed: day 2–6, 47%).

kinds.label: Whether it lasts
kinds.question: Does the change last after help stops, or for good?
kinds.why: Kept from the v10 'How quitting goes' numbers he liked (porn: 74% still watched 70% less three months on; 1 in 6 stopped).

kinds.label: What happened with help, no comparison
kinds.question: What happened to people who got a kind of help, where no study counts people without it?
kinds.why: Added in gates round 2: a with-help result that has no without-help count can't be a what-helps number (rule 12a), but it still answers who quits using what.
